title: Permanence properties of \'etale-smooth local on source-and-target properties: \'etale locality on the source, smooth locality on the target, and postcomposition/permanence for \'etale morphisms

difficulty_reason: The author announces 'We write everything out completely' and proves all four parts in full: (1) uses that the \'etale morphism of pairs (X_i, x_i) \to (X, x) together with id_Y supplies the diagram demanded by part (3) of the \'etale-smooth locality definition, plus the converse from part (1) of the definition; (2) runs the analogous argument with smooth coverings of the target, using that X_i \to X \times_Y Y_i is an isomorphism hence \'etale; (3) builds the square with X \to Y \times_Z X \'etale (\'etale permanence, cited) and Y \to Z smooth, fitting part (3) of the definition for every x; (4) deduces f = pr_Y \circ (f, 1) with (f, 1) \'etale as a section of the \'etale projection (cited), then pr_Y has P by base change and f by part (1). Each part is a separate argument with its own diagram; the assembly is the substance.
